overall_diagnosis: The run failed mainly because the file-organization workflow allowed content misclassification and lacked an exhaustive reconciliation pass: multiple PDFs were moved into incorrect subject folders and at least one expected trapped-ion/QC paper ended up under music_history without being caught before completion. A second, recurring failure mode was verifier detection of stray .docx files outside the intended dataset (e.g., in environment/site-packages or caches), indicating the workflow did not properly scope searches and validation to the dataset root or account for global extension-based checks. Improving dataset-scoped operations plus per-file validation and lightweight PDF text/metadata extraction for topic identification would prevent both misplacements and stray-file verifier failures.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill guidance did not enforce deterministic, content-validated classification and a mandatory end-to-end reconciliation after moves. The agent relied on partial checks (e.g., folder counts) and missed wrong-subject placements and missing/incorrectly placed items. It also failed to anticipate verifiers that scan broadly for allowed extensions, missing stray .docx files outside the target dataset.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a 'dataset-scoped organization protocol' and 'mandatory reconciliation checklist' for taxonomy sorting tasks: (1) define a single ROOT (e.g., /root/papers) and restrict all find/Glob/Grep/moves to ROOT; explicitly forbid scanning /root, ~/.cache, or site-packages and warn that global scans can surface unrelated files. (2) Two-pass workflow: build an inventory of all allowed-extension files under ROOT/all with basenames + quick content snippet, assign a target folder, then move using exact basenames. (3) Reconciliation step before finishing: verify every seen filename exists exactly once in the five target folders, produce a missing/wrong-subject report, and iterate until clean. (4) Final safety scan within ROOT to ensure no allowed extensions remain outside the five folders; if the task’s verifier is known to scan globally, add instructions to detect/mitigate stray extension files introduced by tooling (avoid creating/copying templates; if safe, remove unintended artifacts). Include example shell commands for inventory, diffing, and safe mv.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Accurate sorting depended on quickly extracting enough PDF text/metadata to identify topics, but the workflow likely used insufficient or unreliable signals, leading to multiple subject misclassifications (e.g., QC vs music_history, LLM vs DNA).
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a 'batch PDF topic classification' section: recommend extracting title/abstract/first 1–2 pages via pdftotext or pypdf (with guidance on handling empty extract_text() and scanned/OCR cases), and using lightweight keyword heuristics aligned to the task taxonomy. Provide a batch snippet to generate per-file text previews for human/LLM review prior to moving, and emphasize read-only processing (no rewriting PDFs) during classification.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Verifier failures were triggered by stray .docx files outside the intended folders (likely from installed packages/templates/caches), but the workflow did not warn that filesystem-wide extension checks can penalize unrelated DOCX artifacts created or present in the environment.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add explicit guidance for tasks with filesystem-wide verification: avoid unnecessary package/tool installation that may introduce .docx templates; keep all DOCX-related artifacts confined to the dataset/project directory; and, when safe, locate and remove unintended .docx files outside the allowed folders (or ensure the task workflow never creates them). Include a note to scope searches to the dataset root unless the task explicitly requires global scans.
